online_research_summary.finding: Pydantic v2 generates JSON Schema compliant with JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 and OpenAPI 3.1. Supports WithJsonSchema, SkipJsonSchema, and programmatic field/model-level customization. model_json_schema() returns a jsonable dict; TypeAdapter.json_schema() handles arbitrary types.
online_research_summary.relevance_to_rig: Medium. Useful if Rig wants Python models as the source of truth generating schemas, but reverses the contract-to-schema-to-code direction. Pydantic's Draft 2020-12 output creates a mismatch with Rig's 174 draft-07 schemas.
online_research_summary.risk_or_limitation: Draft mismatch: Pydantic v2 generates Draft 2020-12 schemas, but ALL Rig schemas use draft-07. Using Pydantic's output directly would break schema compatibility. Pydantic's model_json_schema() is not currently used anywhere in Rig.

online_research_summary.finding: Jinja2 is a modern, designer-friendly templating engine for Python with sandboxed execution, template inheritance, filters, and macros. Already installed as a production dependency (jinja2>=3.1.0) but completely unused in the codebase.
online_research_summary.relevance_to_rig: High. Jinja2 is already available as a dormant dependency. Simple deterministic templates can generate Pydantic models, dataclasses, enums, validators, and typed clients from schema JSON. Zero new dependency if used for compiler codegen.
online_research_summary.risk_or_limitation: Template output quality depends entirely on template author quality. No built-in semantic understanding of Pydantic field constraints. Template ordering must be explicitly managed for determinism.

online_research_summary.finding: Ruff is a fast Python linter and formatter compatible with Black. Produces deterministic output given deterministic input. Supports pyproject.toml configuration with explicit line length, quote style, and preview features. Already in Rig's dev dependencies.
online_research_summary.relevance_to_rig: High. Can serve as the post-generation deterministic formatter. Template output can be intentionally unformatted then normalized by ruff, guaranteeing deterministic byte output regardless of template whitespace quirks.
online_research_summary.risk_or_limitation: Ruff format rules can evolve between versions. Format output is deterministic within the same version but not guaranteed across versions. Generator version must include the Ruff version in its provenance fingerprint.

online_research_summary.finding: datamodel-code-generator v0.57.0 generates Pydantic v2 BaseModel, Pydantic v2 dataclasses, standard dataclasses, TypedDict, and msgspec Struct from JSON Schema, OpenAPI 3, GraphQL, JSON/YAML/CSV, Python types, and Python dictionaries. MIT licensed. Handles $ref, allOf, oneOf, anyOf, enums, and nested types. Used by PostHog, Airbyte, Apache Iceberg, OpenAI Codex, vllm, and many others. Supports CI/CD integration via GitHub Action and pyproject.toml configuration.
online_research_summary.relevance_to_rig: High as an optional low-level projection tool. Could generate Pydantic v2 models from Rig's draft-07 JSON Schemas. Rig would own the semantic contract, validation matrix, evidence receipts, and coordination events.
online_research_summary.risk_or_limitation: Would add a new MIT-licensed dependency. Produces opinionated output that may differ from Rig's code style conventions. Generated code quality depends on schema quality. Not suitable as the sole generation tool because it lacks contract-level semantic understanding.

online_research_summary.finding: Hypothesis is the standard Python property-based testing library. Generates random inputs over declared ranges including edge cases. Supports stateful testing, replay of failures, and composable strategies. Not currently installed in Rig.
online_research_summary.relevance_to_rig: High. Could serve as the adversarial validator for generated code, proving that generated models reject invalid inputs and accept valid ones. Strategies would be derived from the semantic contract JSON, not from the generated model's type hints.
online_research_summary.risk_or_limitation: Would add a new Mozilla Public License 2.0 dependency (AGPL-compatible). Requires strategy definitions that match contract semantics, not schema shapes. Property-based tests are non-deterministic by design (but reproducible with fixed seeds).

online_research_summary.finding: cosmic-ray v8.4.6 is a mutation testing tool for Python 3. Mutates source code (operators, constants, control flow) and runs the test suite; if tests still pass against mutated code, reveals weak tests. MIT licensed. Python 3.9+. Not currently installed in Rig.
online_research_summary.relevance_to_rig: Medium. Could serve as an optional CI-only gate to detect whether generated code tests are fake-green. Mutations that survive the validation matrix indicate tests that don't actually enforce contract semantics.
online_research_summary.risk_or_limitation: Expensive to run (full test suite per mutation). Better as an opt-in CI gate than a per-candidate validation check. Adds a new MIT-licensed dependency. Mutation testing is computationally expensive and may not be practical for every compiler run.

online_research_summary.finding: LibCST parses Python as a lossless concrete syntax tree, preserving comments, whitespace, parentheses, and formatting details. Useful for codemods, linters, and source-to-source transformations. BSD-licensed. Not currently installed in Rig.
online_research_summary.relevance_to_rig: Low for fresh codegen. LibCST's strength is preserving existing concrete syntax when modifying existing files, making it valuable for safe codemods on existing code. Overkill for generating fresh Pydantic model files from templates.
online_research_summary.risk_or_limitation: Would add a new BSD-licensed dependency. Overkill for fresh module generation where template output + ruff formatting is simpler and sufficient. Preservation of comments and whitespace is irrelevant when generating new files.

online_research_summary.finding: Python's stdlib ast module can parse Python source to AST nodes and unparse back to source code via ast.unparse (Python 3.9+). Requires zero dependencies. Can validate AST correctness of generated code but formatting output is unpredictable.
online_research_summary.relevance_to_rig: Medium. Available without dependencies for AST validation. ast.parse can verify generated Python is syntactically valid. ast.unparse is not deterministic across Python versions and loses whitespace/comment formatting.
online_research_summary.risk_or_limitation: ast.unparse output is not guaranteed byte-for-byte identical across Python versions. Not suitable for deterministic code generation. Better for validation (parse check) than for generation (unparse step).

git_worktree_available.notes: Git worktrees are already used by Rig's coordination package (WorktreeManager at rig_relay/coordination/worktree_manager.py, 689 lines). Agent/lane isolation uses git worktrees under .rig/relay/worktrees. The compiler can reuse this exact infrastructure for per-candidate validation isolation.

git_worktree_requirement.description: Every candidate must be validated in an isolated Git worktree against the real repository substrate, not just as inert files under .build/. The worktree is where truth happens. The compiler is a staged synthesis ladder: the contract is decomposed into satisfiable slices, each slice's candidates are validated in scratch worktrees, partial successes are promoted to stage worktrees, and the next slice builds on the current stage — not the original HEAD. This prevents the central fake-green risk of cosmetically-valid-but-integration-broken generated artifacts.
git_worktree_requirement.worktree_lifecycle: created → patch_applied → validation_running → failed_reset → failed_reaped; OR → partially_satisfied → promoted_to_stage → next_slice_search; OR → fully_satisfied → accepted → promotion_proposal_emitted → retained_for_review

worktree_lifecycle_states.description: Empty clean worktree checked out at current stage base
Validation matrix executing against real repo substrate
All assertions not met; scratch worktree reset to current stage base
Failed scratch worktree removed after evidence copied to .build/
All assertions for current contract slice satisfied; candidate promoted to next stage
Partial success becomes the base for the next contract slice search
Entire contract satisfied by this candidate
Full contract-satisfying candidate; read-only, retained for human review
Governed promotion proposal emitted to coordination ledger
Accepted worktree cleaned after human checkpoint

contract_slicing.description: The compiler decomposes the semantic contract into ordered satisfiable slices. Each slice is an assertion group. Partial success on slice N promotes the candidate to a stage worktree, which becomes the base for slice N+1. This turns the compiler into staged accumulation instead of a flat monolithic candidate farm.

slice_ordering.description: Every schema_version field in generated output matches the canonical schema file path convention
Every entity in the semantic contract has a corresponding schema definition and Python model
Contract invariants (min, max, pattern, enum, required, additionalProperties, format) are present in schema and enforced by Python validators
All output is content-light: SHA-256 hashes for paths, no raw secrets, no file contents in model dumps
Real artifacts from the existing test corpus round-trip through generated models without data loss or corruption
Invalid JSON, missing required fields, extra forbidden fields, constraint violations all cause proper validation errors

pattern_aggregation.description: After a compiler run completes, the system aggregates all permutation data into structured data products: which schema/template patterns succeeded, which failed, which counterexamples killed multiple candidates, which contract assertions were hardest to satisfy. These data products feed the refinement loop and become the contract_permutation_corpus, schema_pattern_library, template_refinement_backlog, contract_ambiguity_index, and fake_green_failure_catalog.

data_products.description: Complete record of all generated schema/Python permutations with pass/fail/quarantine status and SHA-256 hashes
Schema constraints and structures that repeatedly produced valid candidates across runs
Jinja2 template patterns that caused failures; suggested refinements
Contract assertions that were hardest to satisfy across candidates; may indicate ambiguous contract language
Candidates that passed shallow checks but failed adversarial or worktree validation; the patterns of fake-green success
Counterexamples that killed multiple candidates grouped by failure modality

refinement_loop.description: When a candidate is rejected but close (e.g., passes import but fails adversarial test), the compiler emits a refinement_proposal coordination event with the specific failure, the gate that failed, a diff between accepted schema and rejected candidate, and suggested repair strategies. These proposals are recorded for human review. The next compiler run may use counterexamples from prior runs to generate more adversarial test inputs.

promotion_policy.description: No generated file ever touches canonical repo paths (rig_relay/ or docs/schemas/) until a human-governed promotion step explicitly moves it. Promotion requires: full validation matrix pass, deterministic regeneration match, contract_fit_score at or above acceptance threshold, all coordination events recorded, and explicit human approval with SHA-256 verification.

optional_datamodel_code_generator_path.description: Optionally add as a comparison evaluation gate for regenerating models from an external tool and comparing output to the first-party compiler. Useful for detecting bugs in either generator.

optional_hypothesis_path.description: Optionally add as an adversarial property-based testing gate. Would enable the compiler to generate random inputs over declared contract ranges and verify that generated models reject invalid inputs. Strategies derived from contract JSON, not generated code.

rejected_libcst_for_first_slice.description: LibCST is overkill for generating fresh Pydantic model files. Its strength is preserving existing concrete syntax during codemods on hand-written code. For fresh module generation, Jinja2 template output combined with ruff formatting is simpler and sufficient. Revisit LibCST when the compiler needs to safely modify existing hand-written modules.

rejected_openapi_generator_path.description: OpenAPI Generator requires OpenAPI as input format, but Rig uses JSON Schema as the canonical machine-readable format. It adds a heavy Java-based dependency not well-matched to Rig's artifact ecosystem.

generated_code_imports_but_violates_sema.prevention: Adversarial tests must inject counterexamples derived from the semantic contract, not the generated schema. Property-based strategies must be defined from contract invariants, not model type hints.

generated_schema_accepts_too_much.prevention: Constraint coverage report: every constraint in the contract must appear in the generated schema. Missing constraints cause rejection. Schema must reject inputs the contract says should be rejected.

generated_schema_rejects_valid_artifacts.prevention: Round-trip validation against real artifacts from the existing test corpus. Generated schema must accept all known-valid artifacts that the contract says are valid.

generated_tests_mirror_generated_code.prevention: Tests must be defined from the semantic contract JSON, not from the generated Python. The test file is hand-written and version-controlled separately from generated code. Tests exercise contract invariants, not implementation details.

model_dump_schema_checks_only_field_name.prevention: Round-trip validation must check: minimum, maximum, pattern, enum values, required fields, additionalProperties, format constraints, and type constraints. Any silently dropped constraint causes rejection.

weak_property_strategies.prevention: Hypothesis strategies must be derived from the contract JSON, not from the generated model's type hints. Strategies should target edge cases: boundary values, empty collections, null equivalents, max-length strings, pattern edge cases.

synthetic_fixture_only_acceptance.prevention: The validation matrix must include real artifacts from the existing repository: actual coordination events, actual tool receipts, actual projections. Synthetic fixtures alone are insufficient proof.

failed_candidates_deleted.prevention: The compiler must NEVER delete failed candidate artifacts. All failures are preserved as coordination events with SHA-256 hashes. Failed candidate directories are retained for audit.

duplicate_failures_not_deduped.prevention: The compiler must hash candidate inputs and detect duplicate failures. Only the first instance of each unique failure (same input_hash + same failure_gate) generates a coordination event.

schema_draft_mismatch.prevention: All 174 Rig schemas use draft-07. Generated schemas must also be draft-07. The compiler must reject any schema with a different $schema value. Pydantic v2 generates Draft 2020-12; if Pydantic is ever used for schema generation, its output must be backported to draft-07.

generated_code_without_provenance.prevention: Every generated file must include a header comment with: contract_family_id, contract_version, generator_id, generator_version, generated_at, input_contract_sha256, schema_candidate_sha256. No anonymous generated code in canonical paths.

inert_file_only_validation.prevention: Candidates must never be validated only as inert files under .build/. Every candidate must be applied in an isolated Git worktree and validated against the real repository substrate: real import paths, real package layout, real schema files, real test runner, real pyright/ruff context, real artifact paths, real coordination/CI/receipt conventions. A candidate that passes in a temp directory but fails when applied to the repo must be rejected. This is the single most important fake-green guard because it prevents the compiler from accepting candidates that are cosmetically valid but integration-broken.

contract_ambiguity_risk.prevention: Ambiguous contract language can cause the compiler to accept candidates that satisfy a weak interpretation but violate the intended semantics. The contract_ambiguity_index tracks which assertions are hardest to satisfy across candidates. When the same assertion group fails across multiple unrelated candidates, the contract itself may need refinement — not the generated code. The compiler must emit contract.ambiguity.detected events when assertion groups show high failure rates across independent candidate families, and the contract must be refined before the compiler is rerun.

final_recommendation.exact_next_action: Canonicalize this feasibility assessment as a schema-governed JSON artifact at docs/json/compiler/contract_compiler_feasibility.v1.json and validate it with a contract test at tests/compiler/test_contract_compiler_feasibility_artifact.py. The architecture now requires that every candidate be validated in an isolated Git worktree against the real repository — not as inert files under .build/. Do not start compiler implementation until Coordination Event Ledger Contract v1 and CI Evidence Contract v1 exist.
final_recommendation.release_paper_relevance: This is a publishable architecture: contract-satisfaction compilation with isolated worktree-based validation and preserved candidate failure and permutation evidence. The system treats code generation as a search-and-evaluate loop over a semantic contract, not a one-shot schema-to-code translation. Every accepted or rejected permutation is recorded as a coordination ledger event. Counterexamples are preserved for future adversarial validation. Generated code cannot reach canonical paths without human-governed promotion and full validation matrix pass against the real repository substrate. Critically, candidates are never validated as inert files under .build/ — they are applied in isolated Git worktrees and tested against the real codebase to prevent the central fake-green risk of cosmetically-valid-but-integration-broken generated artifacts. This architecture prevents code generation from becoming fake-green theater.
